perspective:
From Sara Manuelito’s available perspective:

- Sara is a Speech-Language Pathologist. Shirley Whiteplume is her long-time nurse colleague and close friend at a community health center; they have worked together for several years.
- At the funeral of a mutual patient, Sara saw Shirley looking somber and suspected Shirley was deeply affected. Sara told Shirley she knew it was hard and had seen how much Shirley cared for him. Shirley said it had been tough, that she kept thinking if more could have been done, and that it was hard to let go. Sara said they did everything they could and should remember the good care and joy they brought to his life.
- During a coffee break at work, Sara asked to discuss their treatment decisions, saying she sensed Shirley felt burdened by the outcome. Shirley said she felt responsible and wondered if pushing a different approach might have given him a better chance. Sara said they made the best decisions with the information they had and that the burden was too heavy to carry alone. Shirley said she appreciated that but found it hard to accept.
- In a quiet office moment, Sara observed Shirley still reserved and minimally expressive. Sara told her she noticed she was holding back feelings and it was okay to be open. Shirley said she wasn’t sure she could and didn’t want to seem unprofessional or weak. Sara said showing emotions doesn’t make her weak and is healthy among friends. Shirley said Sara might be right and she would try to be more open.
- Later, Sara felt she may have been too harsh, so she apologized for coming on too strong. Shirley said it was a bit much but knew Sara meant well and appreciated the apology. Sara thanked her and said she was there for her. Shirley thanked her and said they should keep talking; it helps.
- After some time, Sara noticed Shirley seemed to be doing better and felt hopeful. She asked how Shirley was feeling. Shirley said she was better thanks to their talks and Sara’s support. Sara offered to spend more time together outside work. Shirley said she would like that and proposed planning something for the weekend.

Sara’s knowledge is limited to these observations, her own actions/intentions/feelings, and what Shirley said aloud; she does not have narrator-only or hidden details about Shirley’s private inner life.
